compiled_state.description:
## The defect

`tests/conftest.py`'s autouse `_no_repo_commits` guard fails a test whose surrounding HEAD
snapshot moved, with:

    Test moved the repo HEAD (X -> Y): it committed into the rebar checkout instead of an
    isolated tmp tracker. Isolate the git writes — ...

Like its sibling `_no_repo_root_leaks`, it is a **before/after snapshot of whole-checkout
state** and cannot tell an in-test mutation from an external one. When the HEAD move comes
from a concurrent `git commit` / rebase / branch switch — the normal case in a detached suite
run, because the agent that launched it keeps working in the same worktree — the message
asserts as fact something that did not happen: the named test did not commit anything, and the
prescribed remedy ("isolate the git writes", "undo the stray commit(s) with git reset --hard")
is wrong and, if followed, destructive.

## Relationship to bug `f0fb-de7a-b315-4508`

`f0fb` proved this exact mechanism deterministically for the *leak* guard (an external `touch`
mid-run produced `6 passed, 1 error` blaming an innocent test) and fixed that guard's message
to name the concurrent-external-writer possibility. This is the identical defect in the
adjacent fixture in the same file.

It was deliberately left out of `f0fb`'s scope: `f0fb`'s own description classifies the
HEAD-move class as KNOWN and separately explained, and the operator scoped that change to the
leak-guard message, the e2e returncode diagnostic, and the docs. But "known" describes the
*class*, not the message — the text still states a falsehood, and multiple recorded incidents
show agents reading it as a real test defect before recognising it. Two on file: "running a
rebase during a background pytest produced 8 spurious failures + 33 errors"; and "an artifact
of my own concurrent git commit ... it attributed to a DIFFERENT test in each of the two runs".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `_no_repo_commits` failure message no longer asserts that the named test committed;
      it names the concurrent-external-writer possibility alongside the in-test one, matching
      the wording `_no_repo_root_leaks` now uses (`tests/_isolation.py::leak_failure_message`).
- [ ] It still tells a genuinely-committing test how to fix itself (the isolation guidance and
      the recovery command are retained, framed as conditional on the test being the cause).
- [ ] The `git reset --hard <sha>` remedy is not presented unconditionally, since following it
      on an external commit destroys a concurrent worktree's work.
- [ ] A RED test proves it, built on the same seam as `leak_failure_message` so both guards'
      text is exercised by the self-test rather than duplicated inline.
- [ ] No detection is weakened — the guard still fails on a real in-test commit.
compiled_state.title: HEAD-move guard message asserts an innocent test committed
